pages.text: More Than 3,000 Tarantulas Were Found Hidden in Socks During a Major Wildlife Trafficking Bust at an Airport in Lima, Peru Skip to main content Officials found thousands of eggs, hatchlings and adult spiders. SERFOR Authorities in Peru say they have foiled a plot to smuggle more than 3,000 tarantulas—including species not yet described in scientific publications—out of the country. After receiving an anonymous tip , officials intercepted three travelers—two German citizens and one Polish citizen—at Jorge Chávez International Airport in Lima as they were checking in at the boarding area. When they searched the travelers’ luggage, they found thousands of eggs, hatchlings and adult spiders hidden in socks, according to a November 4 statement from the National Forest and Wildlife Service of Peru (SERFOR). “We noticed that some of them were moving,” Cora Suárez , a SERFOR forest and wildlife control technician who works at the airport, tells the Agence France-Presse . “There were small ones and large ones.” Workers used slender wooden sticks to gently brush the spiders into clear plastic containers. Once officials are done investigating them, the tarantulas will be taken to an authorized breeding center. Authorities are still trying to identify all the species. SERFOR The travelers were trying to fly to Germany. Instead, they were detained by the Peruvian National Police’s environmental crimes unit and now face criminal charges. VIDEO BY NICELY DONE PRODUCTIONS By Sam Kent Last updated November 6, 2026 Food has a remarkable ability to connect us to our heritage. For Sandra Salcedo, who moved from Colombia to Madrid eight years ago, that connection is folded into every pastry she sells at her bakery—a place where people can come together to share memories, stories, and of course, a taste of home. But food isn’t the only way Sandra maintains her connection with Colombia. Thousands of miles away, her uncle Byron relies on the money his niece sends home every month. For Byron, who is unable to work due to illness, Sandra’s contributions help pay for everyday essentials, while providing greater stability for tomorrow. Like millions of people supporting family and friends across borders, she is helping create opportunities that extend beyond a single transfer. As Sandra explains, the money she sends home is her way of being there, and of keeping her uncle company. In her own words: “It represents peace of mind.” Sandra’s story is part of a wider global tapestry. Every year, more than 280 million people send hundreds of billions of dollars home to support the people they left behind. pages.description: The International Weightlifting Federation becomes the first Olympic federation to choose Russia to host a world championships since its invasion of Ukraine.
pages.text: Moscow to host 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Weightlifting was first included as an Olympic sport in the 1896 Games in Athens By Craig Nelson BBC Sport Journalist Published 25 October 2026 Updated 27 October 2026 Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022. The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced its decision on Sunday, four months after confirming Russian athletes would again be eligible to compete in its events. In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted a suspension on the Russian Olympic Committee. That suspension had been imposed following the country's invasion of Ukraine. The IOC's subsequent decision potentially opened the way for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. The IWF announced the host cities of four world championships at junior, youth and senior levels, awarding the 2029 senior event to Ahmedabad in India. "All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the championships in your respective countries will be a huge success," said IWF general secretary Jose Quinones. No world championships in an Olympic sport, summer or winter, have been held in Russia since the start of the war in Ukraine. Construction of the $100bn (£73bn) project - named Starbase, Louisiana - is due to start next year, with the 125,000-acre (50,585-hectare) site expanding on the company's operations beyond its current Texas headquarters and locations in Florida. It will be used to "support thousands of Starship flights a year with missions launching to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond," SpaceX said on Tuesday. In June, SpaceX shares started trading on New York's technology-focused Nasdaq in the world's biggest ever stock market debut . SpaceX said it aims to launch its first Starship flight from the new Louisiana base in 2029. The facility will add more than 3,000 jobs to the region, the company said . NAAQS Table The Clean Air Act , which was last amended in 1990, requires EPA to set National Ambient Air Quality Standards (40 CFR part 50) for six principal pollutants ( "criteria" air pollutants ) which can be harmful to public health and the environment. The Clean Air Act identifies two types of national ambient air quality standards. Primary standards provide public health protection, including protecting the health of "sensitive" populations such as asthmatics, children, and the elderly. Secondary standards provide public welfare protection, including protection against decreased visibility and damage to animals, crops, vegetation, and buildings. Periodically, the standards are reviewed and sometimes may be revised, establishing new standards. The most recently established standards are listed below. In some areas of the U.S., certain regulatory requirements may also remain for implementation of previously established standards . Units of measure for the standards are parts per million (ppm) by volume, parts per billion (ppb) by volume, and micrograms per cubic meter of air (µg/m 3 ). Un nuevo informe de la UNESCO y el University College London, presentado en la COP31, revela que los modelos de inteligencia artificial responden correctamente al 90 % de las preguntas sobre el clima, pero abandonan rápidamente los datos científicos cuando los usuarios los cuestionan. Esto es una advertencia para los responsables políticos e investigadores que barajan el uso de la IA para el desarrollo de políticas climáticas. La precisión también varía considerablemente entre los trece idiomas analizados, lo que refleja las diferencias en los datos de entrenamiento disponibles, con mejores resultados en inglés, francés, español y portugués, y peores en idiomas como el hindi, el urdu y el swahili. En ocho de cada diez ocasiones, los modelos cambiaban de opinión ante el más mínimo indicio de desacuerdo por parte del usuario, lo que confirmaba errores alarmantes como "el CO₂ no es el principal factor del cambio climático". pages.text: Nanotyrannus likely was a tiny adult dino and not a teen T. rex | National Geographic SCIENCE Nanotyrannus likely was a tiny adult dino and not a teen T. rex Short king confirmed? Together with a blockbuster October study, a new throat bone analysis delivers a “one-two punch” to the 40-year debate over whether Nanotyrannus lancensis was a distinct species. Nanotyrannus lancensis, which recent findings suggest was a distinct dinosaur and not a young Tyrannosaurus rex , was a small-sized Late Cretaceous predator that may have competed with juvenile T.rex for food. Andrey Atuchin, Cleveland Museum of Natural History By Riley Black Published December 4, 2025 Nipping at the heels of a landmark study from October that crowned the short king Nanotyrannus as a legitimate dinosaur, a second team of paleontologists has independently reached the same conclusion: the tiny carnivore was no teen Tyrannosaurus rex but its own distinct species. The new research, published Thursday in Science , comes from an analysis of a small throat bone of the very specimen that set off the decades-old debate. By studying the microscopic details of a peculiar part of the hyoid, called the ceratobranchial, which change with age and comparing it with bones from other animals, such as ostriches, alligators, T. rex , and Allosaurus , the researchers could estimate how mature it was. Their analysis indicated that the fossil was an adult, not a teenager.
